subject: Science
text: Which group correctly shows only vertebrates?
solution: Frogs, lizards and eagles have backbones.

subject: Science
text: Which plant structure mainly carries water from roots to leaves?
solution: Xylem transports water and mineral salts upward.

subject: Science
text: Cactus plants have thick, fleshy stems. Name the main function of this adaptation.
solution: Succulent stems store water in dry habitats.

subject: Science
text: Which statement about mammals is true?
options: They produce milk for their young
answer: They produce milk for their young
solution: Mammals feed their young with milk.

subject: Science
text: Which is a characteristic of bacteria?
options: make their own food using chlorophyll always
solution: Bacteria are unicellular and microscopic.

subject: Science
text: State the three common states of matter.
solution: Matter commonly exists as solid, liquid and gas.

subject: Science
text: Which process changes water vapour to liquid water?
solution: Cooling water vapour causes condensation.

subject: Science
text: A penguin has a thick layer of fat under its skin. This helps it to __.
solution: Fat acts as insulation in cold environments.

subject: Science
text: Name one non-flowering plant commonly found in gardens.
solution: Ferns and mosses are non-flowering plants.

subject: Science
text: Which statement about gases is correct?
options: fixed shape but not fixed volume
no fixed shape and no fixed volume
fixed volume but no fixed shape
answer: no fixed shape and no fixed volume
solution: Gases expand to fill their container.

subject: Science
text: Which process in the water cycle requires heat from the Sun?
solution: Heat causes water to evaporate.

subject: Science
text: Water droplets forming on the outside of a cold drink can is due to __.
solution: Water vapour in air condenses on the cold surface.

subject: Science
text: Which shows a complete life cycle with metamorphosis?
solution: Frog has egg → tadpole → adult (metamorphosis).

subject: Science
text: Which stage of a butterfly eats the most and grows rapidly?
solution: Feeding and growth occur mainly at larva stage.

subject: Science
text: Name the process when a solid changes directly into a gas.
solution: E.g., dry ice sublimates.

subject: Science
text: Clouds form mainly because of __.
solution: Water vapour condenses into tiny droplets.

subject: Science
text: Which sequence shows human development?
solution: Correct developmental order.

subject: Science
text: State one way to speed up the drying of wet clothes apart from sunlight.
solution: Greater airflow increases evaporation.

subject: Science
text: Which is a reversible change?
solution: Freezing can reverse melting.

subject: Science
text: Name the process by which plants make food.
solution: Chlorophyll + sunlight + CO₂ + water → glucose + oxygen.

subject: Science
text: Which organ mainly absorbs water from undigested food?
solution: Large intestine absorbs water and minerals.

subject: Science
text: Which structure contracts to help us breathe in?
solution: Diaphragm contracts and moves downwards during inhalation.

subject: Science
text: Which blood vessel carries blood away from the heart?
solution: Arteries carry blood away; veins carry blood to the heart.

subject: Science
text: Most digestion and absorption of nutrients occur in the __.
solution: Small intestine is the main site of digestion and absorption.

subject: Science
text: Name the gas taken in during respiration.
solution: Oxygen is needed for energy release.

subject: Science
text: Which part of a leaf allows gases to enter and leave the plant?
solution: Stomata are pores for gas exchange.

subject: Science
text: Which component of blood carries oxygen?
solution: Haemoglobin in RBCs carries oxygen.

subject: Science
text: State one function of saliva in digestion.
solution: Salivary amylase digests starch; saliva moistens food.

subject: Science
text: Air sacs in the lungs are called __.
solution: Alveoli are the site of gas exchange.

subject: Science
text: Name the organ that pumps blood around the body.
solution: The heart pumps blood through blood vessels.

subject: Science
text: Which force opposes motion between two surfaces in contact?
solution: Friction resists motion.

subject: Science
text: An object falls to the ground when dropped because of __.
solution: Gravity pulls objects toward Earth.

subject: Science
text: Name one material that a magnet can attract.
solution: Magnets attract magnetic materials such as iron and steel.

subject: Science
text: To reduce friction between moving parts, we can __.
solution: Lubricants reduce friction.

subject: Science
text: Which shows a pair of unlike magnetic poles?
solution: Unlike poles attract (N to S).

subject: Science
text: Name the measuring instrument used to measure force.
solution: A spring balance measures force in newtons.

subject: Science
text: A student measured the force needed to pull a block over different surfaces.
solution: Largest force needed → greatest friction.

subject: Science
text: Name one simple machine that helps lift heavy loads more easily.
solution: Simple machines provide mechanical advantage.

subject: Science
text: A sharp knife cuts better than a blunt one mainly because it has __.
solution: Smaller area → higher pressure for same force.

subject: Science
text: State the effect on two magnets if their like poles are brought close together.
solution: Like poles repel.

subject: Science
text: Shadows are formed because light __.
solution: Straight-line travel causes regions with no light (shadows).

subject: Science
text: Which surface reflects most light?
solution: White surfaces reflect more light than dark surfaces.

subject: Science
text: Metals are good conductors of heat. Name one use based on this property.
solution: Conduct heat quickly to food or away from devices.

subject: Science
text: Which material is the best thermal insulator?
solution: Wood is a poor conductor; hence a good insulator.

subject: Science
text: Sound is produced when objects __.
solution: Vibrations produce sound.

subject: Science
text: Name one factor that affects the size of a shadow.
answer: distance between object and screen|distance between object and light source|angle of light|size of object
solution: Changing distances or angles changes shadow size.

subject: Science
text: Which method of heat transfer does not require a medium?
solution: Radiation can occur through a vacuum.

subject: Science
text: State one way to reduce echoes in a hall.
answer: add carpets|install curtains|use sound-absorbing panels|add cushions
solution: Soft materials absorb sound.

subject: Science
text: Which change increases the brightness of a bulb in a simple circuit?
solution: Higher voltage increases brightness.

subject: Science
text: Hot air rises. Name the heat transfer process involved.
solution: Warm, less dense air rises; cooler air sinks.

subject: Science
text: In a simple series circuit, the bulb does not light. Which could be the reason?
solution: An open switch breaks the circuit.

subject: Science
text: Which material is a good electrical conductor?
solution: Metals like copper conduct electricity well.

subject: Science
text: Name the type of circuit where components are connected one after another in a single loop.
solution: Single path for current → series circuit.

subject: Science
text: Adding another identical bulb in parallel will make each bulb __.
solution: In a parallel circuit each bulb is connected across the full supply voltage. Adding another identical bulb in parallel increases the total current drawn from the source but does not change the voltage across each bulb - so each bulb remains the same brightness.

subject: Science
text: Which is an example of potential energy?
solution: Stored elastic potential energy.

subject: Science
text: Name the energy conversion in a battery-powered torch when switched on.
answer: chemical to electrical to light|chemical → electrical → light
solution: Chemical energy in battery → electrical → light (and heat).

subject: Science
text: Which is a safe practice when using electricity?
solution: Damaged insulation is dangerous.

subject: Science
text: Give one example of a renewable source of energy.
solution: Renewable sources can be naturally replenished.

subject: Science
text: A closed switch in a simple circuit will cause the bulb to __.
solution: Closed switch completes the circuit.

subject: Science
text: State the main form of energy produced by a ringing alarm clock.
solution: The alarm produces sound energy.

subject: Science
text: In a fair test, which variable should be changed?
solution: Only the manipulated variable is changed.

subject: Science
text: When investigating the effect of light on plant growth, the height of the plant is the __.
solution: Height responds to the presence/absence of light.

subject: Science
text: Write a suitable hypothesis: Plants with more light grow __ than plants with less light.
solution: A testable prediction relating light to growth.

subject: Science
text: A student recorded plant heights over 3 weeks.

subject: Science
text: State one variable that should be kept the same when testing how temperature affects the time for sugar to dissolve in water.
answer: amount of sugar|volume of water|stirring rate|type of sugar
solution: Control variables ensure a fair test.

subject: Science
text: On a graph, the manipulated variable is usually plotted on the __.
solution: Independent variable on x-axis; dependent on y-axis.

subject: Science
text: After an experiment, what should a conclusion be based on?
solution: Conclusions must be supported by the results.

subject: Science
text: Which improves the reliability of results?
solution: Repeats reduce random errors.

subject: Science
text: Name a suitable instrument to measure volume of a liquid accurately in the lab.
solution: Use a measuring/graduate cylinder for liquid volume.

subject: Science
text: From the table: Time (s): 0, 5, 10, 15. Temperature (°C): 25, 28, 30, 31. What is the temperature at 10 s?
solution: Read directly from the table: 30 °C at 10 s.

subject: Science
text: In a simple food chain: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake. The frog is a __.
solution: Grasshopper is primary; frog feeds on it (secondary).

subject: Science
text: Which is a non-living factor in a habitat?
solution: Temperature is abiotic (non-living).

subject: Science
text: Name one adaptation of a fish that helps it move in water.
solution: Streamlining reduces water resistance; fins aid movement.

subject: Science
text: If the number of snakes decreases, which population is likely to increase first?
solution: Fewer snakes → less predation on frogs.

subject: Science
text: State one way humans can help conserve water in daily life.
answer: take shorter showers|turn off tap when brushing|fix leaks
solution: Reduce wastage to conserve water.

subject: Science
text: Which activity most directly causes air pollution?
solution: Burning releases smoke and harmful gases.

subject: Science
text: In a food chain, organisms that make their own food are called __.
solution: Plants are producers.

subject: Science
text: Mangrove trees have breathing roots mainly to __.
options: anchor the tree in soft mud
solution: Pneumatophores help in gas exchange.

subject: Science
text: A survey counted organisms in a pond.
solution: Algae are most numerous (likely producers).

subject: Science
text: State one reason why we should conserve biodiversity.
solution: Biodiversity supports ecosystem stability and resources.
